open_assumptions: Contract 1.4.0 shape assumed from the PRD: reviewResult gains reviewers[] with reviewer_id, transport, session_id, verdict (approved|blocked|null), findings[], launched_at (nullable), accepted_at (nullable), status; each finding gains reviewer (string). Field names beyond the PRD's review.json entry (reviewer_id, session_id, verdict, accepted_at) are my choice: transport, findings, launched_at, status.

Both reviewResult and runInputs projections carry contract_version 1.4.0 (following the 1.3.0 precedent of one shared version literal); fixtures use a single CONTRACT_VERSION constant if the adapter keeps inputs at 1.3.0.

Per-reviewer status values used in fixtures follow the adapter lane's in-progress receipt vocabulary seen read-only in its worktree: succeeded (approved run), accepted, blocked (also for deadline/rejection, then with verdict null), superseded, needs_reconciliation. The viewer derives 'blocked' vs 'timed out or rejected' from status plus verdict and renders unknown status values verbatim.

The existing top-level reviewer.session_id stays in the payload (additive contract); for two-reviewer runs the raw section's reviewer_session_id is the joined session list, as the adapter lane's review.json writes it, while the snapshot review node's session_id is the first reviewer's (the workflow id pattern rejects a joined string). The spec does not assert the review node's session for two-reviewer runs.

The legacy fill for pre-1.4.0 exports is assumed to be reviewer_id 'review', status succeeded/blocked from the verdict, accepted_at = reviewed_at, launched_at null; the spec asserts only id, verdict and the 'completion file accepted' wording for it.

Seeded 1.4.0 run-state files carry version '1.4.0', plan.reviewers [{reviewer_id, prompt}] and the review section with reviewers[]; export_state.py/server field names may differ and would surface at the combined candidate.

Worker-phase browser evidence for viewer-two-reviewers and all existing scenarios is absent in this lane (config-load failure on the 1.3.0 contract); every scenario is expected to pass only at the combined candidate.
I read (never edited) the adapter lane's worktree to align field names; contracts/, server/, workflow/ and features/ were not touched.

adapter.summary: Implemented PRD_PARALLEL_REVIEWERS slice B on the controller, contracts and server adapter. Contracts: reviewCompletion.schema.json 1.2.0 (node_id ^review(-[a-z0-9-]{1,32})?$), feature.schema.json 2.1.0 (optional reviewers list), contracts/projects reviewResult 1.4.0 (reviewers entries, reviewer tag on every finding, unanimous approval rules; runInputs unchanged at 1.3.0), examples, READMEs and both contract tests updated, JSON schemas regenerated with npm run contracts:export. Controller: workflow/prompts/review.md holds the built-in brief; review_prompt(runtime, patch, reviewer) appends the fixed blocks to any brief; sessions.py adds reviewer ids (plan_reviewers, review_node); prepare --reviewer <id>=<brief> pins plan.reviewers; launch.py validates feature 2.1.0 reviewers (unique, not a lane, not reserved, brief exists and non-empty) and keeps 2.0.0/1.0.0 files on the default reviewer. automatic.py launches every reviewer over the shared review-worktree, wait_reviews polls every receipt with per-reviewer deadlines, per-reviewer status files automatic-review-<id>.json plus the combined automatic-review.json (the default reviewer's own status is merged into the combined file so slice A file names are unchanged), _decide over the set (unanimous approval; any block, unresolved P0/P1, rejected file or expiry blocks at once), combined review.json with reviewers entries and reviewer-tagged unioned findings, every reviewer stopped after the decision with superseded statuses, independence check across workers and reviewers, print fallback one job per reviewer in parallel. interactive.py: per-reviewer session names, files, attach-one --node review-<id>, one Claude: reviewer <id> pane per reviewer in declared order each split right of the previous; resume rebinds receipts and a reviewer interrupted before its receipt goes to needs_reconciliation with nothing relaunched. pipeline.py: check_review validates the reviewers list and the reviewer tag, manual review --reviewer <id> --review-file stores <node>.imported.json and combines once every declared reviewer is imported, approve is refused until then. export_state.py 1.4.0 adds review.reviewers (id, transport, session id, verdict, findings, launched_at, accepted_at, status) and finding.reviewer; server/projects.ts accepts exports 1.0.0-1.4.0 and fills a one-entry reviewers list named review for older exports on the unchanged reviews/<attempt> route. Example briefs in features/project-workflows/reviewers/ (general.md, coverage.md) with a README note; RUNBOOK, CHEATSHEET, workflow/README and contract READMEs updated. Tests: every reviewer test in test_automatic runs with one and with two reviewers (native and print); ParallelReviewerScenarios covers two-approve, one-blocks, p1-anywhere, one-times-out, wrong-node, shared-identity and interrupted-launch; default-reviewer is asserted by the single-reviewer classes; manual-import and declared-reviewer prepare/launch validation live in test_lanes; test_interactive covers per-reviewer sessions and panes; test_export covers 1.4.0 entries; server/projects.test.ts covers a two-reviewer export and the legacy fill. Checks executed in this worktree (after npm ci to obtain the pinned dependencies; no new dependencies): workflow-unit (.venv python -m unittest discover -s workflow -t .): 195 tests OK; shared-contract (npm run test:contracts): 18 pass, 0 fail; backend-regression (npm run test:unit): 130 pass, 0 fail; backend-build (npm run build): exit 0; additionally npx tsx --test server/projects.test.ts: 35 pass, 0 fail. Not executed: the section 8 live smoke test, the panes (live) and viewer-two-reviewers scenarios, and any Playwright suite (UI-owned). Nothing committed.
open_assumptions: Only reviewResult moves to contract 1.4.0; runInputs keeps contract_version 1.3.0 because its shape is unchanged. The UI fixture tests/project-workflows/fixtures.ts still projects reviewResult as 1.3.0 without reviewers and must be updated by the UI worker (it compiles, since validators take unknown, but fails at runtime).
With several reviewers, review.json 'reviewer' and the served reviewer.session_id list every reviewer's session id comma-separated in declared order; reviewers[] is the per-reviewer record.

The default reviewer's per-reviewer status is merged into automatic-review.json (no automatic-review-review.json) so a feature without reviewers keeps exactly slice A's file names; declared reviewers get automatic-review-<id>.json beside the combined file.

Per-reviewer status vocabulary: pending, launching, running, accepted, blocked, superseded, succeeded, needs_reconciliation; a deadline is recorded as blocked with a 'deadline exhausted' error, and the export maps statuses to accepted/blocked/superseded/pending (no separate expired value).

review.json is written on a deadline or rejected file only when at least one other reviewer's verdict was already accepted (retaining it, verdict blocked); with no accepted verdict no review.json is written, as before; identity, worktree or evidence refusals never record a partial review.
Reviewer id 'review' is reserved for the implicit default and cannot be declared in feature.json; declared reviewers always own review-<id>.
Manual mode: review without --reviewer is accepted only for a run with the single default reviewer; imports are stored as <node>.imported.json and each imported file must itself be approved.

interrupted-launch: on resume the reviewers that were launched are rebound and left running (not stopped) and the run stays at needs_reconciliation; the operator stops them by id and starts a new run.
features/parallel-reviewers/ was not touched (outside ownership); its own feature.json declares no reviewers, so this run's review uses the built-in reviewer.
